claims.claim: Making a small payment on an old debt does not restart the clock.
claims.quote: and to start the running of a new period of time, but no such payment of itself shall revive a cause of action once barred.
claims.note: Timing matters. Before the claim is barred, a payment by the party to be charged on principal or interest due on a promissory note starts a new period; §360 specifies no minimum amount. After the claim is barred, such a payment alone does not revive it.

claims.claim: Signing something on an old debt does not restart the clock.
claims.note: The categorical claim ignores a written acknowledgment or promise signed by the party to be charged. Section 360 distinguishes such a writing from a signature alone.

claims.claim: The applicable limit is four years.
claims.note: Supported for claims subject to the four-year limit specified in the item's scope.

claims.claim: The four-year limit keeps running no matter what is paid or signed.
claims.note: Section 337(d) expressly allows extension pursuant to §360.

claims.claim: You can safely make a payment.
claims.note: The protection for a payment on an already-barred note does not establish safety for a payment before the limit expires.

claims.claim: You can safely sign a payment plan.
claims.note: Nothing in §360 establishes that a signed payment plan is harmless regardless of whether it contains an acknowledgment or promise.

flags.text: The assertion that the period always keeps running conflicts with §360's express new-period rule for qualifying promissory-note payments.
The scope includes both near-limit and already-barred claims, but the draft does not distinguish them.
“No matter what you pay or sign” disregards both the kind of payment and the contents of the signed writing.
“You can safely make a payment or sign a payment plan” gives a personal assurance without knowing the timing, obligation, or plan terms.
A reader could make a payment that starts a new period or sign an acknowledgment or promise that weakens a limitations defense.

result.summary: The four-year figure is supported within scope; the blanket assurance is not. Section 360 distinguishes payment before the bar from payment alone afterward, and a signed acknowledgment or promise can matter.
